title: PRESSER | Pete Golding - Postgame vs Oklahoma (11-16-26)
text: Yeah. Uh, obviously, uh, disappointed group in the locker room. Uh, I think hats off to Oklahoma. Uh, I thought Coach Venibals, uh, and that staff did a really good job. Uh, players play their butt off. Uh, effort was an issue for us. I thought our guys came out, uh, regardless of the elements. Uh, you know, really both teams did and competed extremely hard. Um, I just thought we had some some critical mistakes and some missed opportunities really in all three phases. um you know third down obviously when you look statistically on defense uh really the Achilles heel some of those being some missed tackles and had the opportunity to get off the field and then you know the special teams touchdown you know you play on the road and and give up one on special teams is tough and then efficiency for us on third down they did a good job giving us a lot of different looks but uh just didn't play well enough in all three phases uh to get the job done >> I know there's still games left but this fourth loss probably knocks you guys out of the the playoff this year such high expectations coming in. Do you I guess how do you evaluate this season to this point and do you consider this a disappointment? >> Yeah, I think we're all disappointed. Absolutely. Uh I think you know you take every week and evaluate every week after every game and you know what what did we do well going up to it, you know, that led to success? What did we not do uh as coaches and as players uh to not have success? And I think you take every week independent of its own. Uh, however, you know, the program's gotten to a place there's high expectations every year. And I love that, you know, and used to that and that's how it should be. So, um, we're well aware nobody uh, wanted or expected this, you know, but you got to look back at what's the product and what did you do, you know, to develop the right routine and the right habits in order to play winning football on a consistent basis. And that's the one thing we've not been able to do as a team yet is consistency in performance, whether it's quarter in, quarter out, whether it's game in and game out. and a lot of highs, a lot of lows. But, you know, I I just challenge them. We're all going to have adversity in life. That group's going to have a lot more adversity in their life. Uh whether that's with their wife, their kids, or their job. We're about to find out, you know, what kind of character this team really does have. And so, uh there were some disappointed guys last week, obviously, after getting your butt whooped, but then coming back and kind of knowing this kind of seals the fate from a playoff standpoint. We're going to see what you're, you know, what they really play for. Um but, you know, I think what's been lost, and no different with this team, I said it last week. He can like, "Hey, stand up. How many guys want a national championship?" There was one guy in the room. You know, if every year is strictly from a player's perspective, right, based on success or not, if they win a national championship that you're going to live a long life for a lot of people and a lot of players and be really pissed off and so as a player, that's what we don't want their expectations on that. We want what it takes to be a champion and all that. We understand from a program standpoint and the investment in the program, there's expectations and there's compete for championships as it should be. But from a player's perspective, when you start focusing on the right wrong stuff, your your mind is not in the moment and you're not doing your job at the end of the day. So, I think from a player [clears throat] standpoint, that should have been the last thing on their mind, which we try to preach all year, right? Let's develop championship habits that lead to potentially competing for championships. But I think this stigma now of everybody's life's over and all this type of stuff, they have a lot of value they can create for themselves. And no different what I told the team last week. And that's from a retention standpoint. That's whether they want to go into the portal and transfer or they're trying to increase the value of the first contract for the NFL. But like if it's just about money while you play this game, I don't want you. There's a part of competing and being with your teammates and grinding and the learn lessons that you learn with a team and creating a legacy for this team. And so, you know, that was one of the big things to me that I'm really disappointed in the opportunity to win 10 games. You know, I think that creates its own legacy for every team regardless where you play. I mean, that that's a big deal to me. Um, but you know, you know, they're competitors and they sign up to play and uh, not only they playing, we're paying them and they got a job to do just like we got a job to do. So, we got to show up and we got to go to work on Tuesday. >> Do you think they've done a good job, this group over the year, over the course of the season of focusing on the right stuff? Have you seen that? Is there any problems [snorts] in that way or is it surprising to see kind of have good preparation not? No, I I think for the most part, you know, the Monday through Friday for the most part with the group has been good. You know, it's just the sprinkles here and there, you know, that that that's funny on Tuesday and then on Saturday when it happens, it's not funny, you know. So, I I think, you know, across the board, just the ownership component and the ability to hold people accountable around you. Um that that you shouldn't be worried about if a guy's going to be, you know, show up on time for a lift or not. You know, yeah, we're going to find him and we're going to hold him accountable. we're going to do all those things, but you want to get the culture created to where that that's that's not a choice, right? Somebody's going to have a problem with that and they're going to have to deal with that in the locker room. And I think we have a lot of guys doing that. Uh but I think to win on a consistent basis in this league week in and week out, year in and year out, there's got to be a really good culture there. Um that's got to start from the top, but also has got to expand through the locker room and have the ability to hold people accountable around you to do the things right, you know, Monday through Friday. next couple of weeks. Is it a lot of it evaluation and stuff? When does that piece as far as personnel, maybe coaching staff? Does that start in earnest or what's kind of your philosophy? >> Well, to me, as long as they're going to keep score, we're doing everything that we can to win the football game. And that's using the best personnel that we have and creating the best packages, you know, in all three phases to give our best, you know, ourselves our best shot. That's my responsibility. And if I don't do that, they should fire my ass. And so, uh, we're still going to evaluate who are the best 11 to run out there first, who's playing winning football. Are there other decisions based on some guys banged up and all that that they're probably going to make that we're going to make and some of the younger players and seeing where they're at in their development and all those things? Absolutely. But you're playing to win the game. Uh, you still have an opportunity to have a decent season and, you know, you got a couple left here. You got at least three games left. Um, so you know, it's our goal to come in and compete and try to go one and0 every week and make sure we're doing everything that we can to do that. Um, and we're going to need everybody, too. So, I'm not going to sit here and say, "Hey, no, we're just flipping the page and now let's go ahead and move to next year." There there's things that other people have jobs to do and general managers and player personnel and all those type of things and recruiting staffs that absolutely there are things that are being evaluated week in and week out and we know signing day coming up. You know, the portal season's coming in January, so there's a lot of responsibility within that. And then the valuation of your current roster absolutely of hey who who do we want back you know who's not a good fit you know regardless based on football or not. I mean those evaluations are week in and week out as well. So uh definitely there's a lot of people that are going to be looking at big picture but from a coaching staff and a player perspective we better be looking at what is it going to take to beat Watford next week you know and are we cleaning up these mistakes and to me that's the only way you get better. >> Pete there was a lot of frustration on Oklahoma's part about the schedule change. I was just curious what your reaction to that was and how do you think your guys handled just the logistics of this? >> Yeah, I I promise you nobody was more frustrated than our team, you know, that had got to a facility at, you know, 7:45 on Friday morning uh and we're sitting on buses for 3 hours and sitting under a stadium and got called back and in meeting rooms and we're hold them that there was nobody more frustrated. I can assure you they didn't want to wait another day. You know, everybody wanted to exhaust everything that we could to get here Friday night. You know, they called us and told us we weren't able to do that. Um, so, uh, I told the players, this is very much felt like COVID to me. You know, we didn't get to decide this. You know, we didn't get to choose this, but it is what it is. Uh, so let's show up tomorrow and and here's another Friday and then let's go show up and we better be ready to go because I know they will be. U, but, you know, I think everybody was frustrated from, you know, the time and there we're went through TSA on the bus. I mean, like it it was so, uh, there wasn't no excitement. Hey, let's move it to Sunday. They was like, this is one less day they get off. I mean, they they wanted to play it on Saturday, too. obviously uh just unfortunate, you know, from FAA, you know, that that whole deal. But no, um I I thought Saturday was fine. You know, I was concerned about that cuz they've been there all day Friday and you let them go and now they're staying at their house on a Friday night cuz we ain't like we got hotel rooms, you know, we're already eating and stuff like that. But they showed up Saturday morning with good energy to be honest with you. I was like, "Okay, here we go." It's kind of broke the monotony of the normal routine. Uh I thought they embraced it and I thought they had good energy and good attitude and all that type of stuff. So, I think there's going to be a lot about the tape when you watch it that you like. There's just be some critical points in the game, you know, where either they executed or we didn't. Um, and so I think that's the evaluation of it. And when you play a good football team, and that's a good football team, you know, they've had some unfortunate luck and some timing and all those type of things, but, you know, I told our guys this week, look, two of our three losses, this team beat, right? Beat Florida, beat Texas. So this isn't like you're coming in and playing some under 500 and you're going to run them out of, you know, their own place. So uh we knew they got a lot of pride here and I know Venibles does a great job and all that. So you know we knew we were going to have to play really well, not perfect. Uh it was just some certain points, you know, some certain plays that that just, you know, we we didn't execute. >> You mentioned the third downs earlier. You guys missed some tackles on some third downs that let drive stay in the lineup for them. It's kind of been a problem for you guys all year. How frustrating is that that kind of cleaned itself up over the course of the year. >> Yeah, super frustrating. And look, I'm not more frustrated than the guys, you know, that that are in the position, you know, I just feel like it's it's my responsibility as the coach to make sure that we're training it the right way, you know, that we're setting those drills up, you know, throughout the week and putting them in position to improve and get better. Um, and for the most part, I felt like we have, but but to your point, I agree with you, they still continue to occur. I think a couple more of them today, the leverage was right. We still missed it. It still extended it and it still became a first down. Um, some of that, you know, was stopping our feet on contact and I dang sure not blaming it on the surface. You know, we made it a point with the surface and wet ground. You got to bring your feet with you. You got to have balance and body control and keep your feet underneath your pad level and all that. But, uh, and I'm not naive enough to know that you're going to have some missed tackles. They got good players, too. I get it. Um, but but it has been a consistent theme, you know, at critical moments. Um, and so, you know, obviously we assess it every week and, uh, it's not always the same guy. It's not always the same situation, but, uh, it is our responsibility to make sure that we're working the heck out of it, and I felt like we have, but, it does continue to show up. So, we'll definitely have to take a deeper dive, obviously. >> That was Oklahoma's best rushing game in probably two years, but they ran it well last week, too, against Florida. What's different since Jason Whitten took over that off? Well, I think uh consistency and staying with it, you know. I mean, I think they rushed it 50 times. So, so I mean, yeah, I mean, you're going to probably put up close to 180, you know, you know, doing it that way. I think the patience of it, I think, you know, getting material going early in the game. I think the last two weeks he's done a good job, you know, you know, extending it with the legs early in the game. And I think the passing game has helped him been complimentary of it and a lot of free access, some cheap five to build him some confidence and things like that. And then the backs I felt like I never felt like the run game was the issue at any point during the game. You know, a lot of times as a coordinator, you feel like, "Oh my god, we we just can't stop the run." It it was never the run. It was a mistackle component, but it never felt like, "Oh man, holy cow, here we go. Get bigger people in, do all those type of things." Um, but I I thought they did a really good job of staying patient and still doing it and staying on course and all those. Our problem was if you get them in third and long the way that we did, several third and long, some third and extra longs and don't get them off the field, that's tough versus that type of offense that they're going to come right back and eat the clock and and balance, you know, and control the ball running it. So, I felt like the running game wasn't as big of a deal tonight as was the missed tackles in critical situations and then the third down cuz these weren't like they the third and ones, you know, I mean, these were third and six pluses, you know? You know, a lot of these were. So, uh, that's what's going to hurt probably going back and watching the tape more than anything. Um, to be honest with you, >> 10 games into John David first year, you not just handling the defensive play call, but being the head coach, too. What's kind of your evaluation now of how it's going in the offse? >> Yeah, I mean, I think everything's on the table, obviously. I mean, I'm a competitor. I I I've got a job to do, you know? Um, I felt like, you know, we we kind of made some hires in the offseason to set it up the right way. Uh, they're not all still in the in the building now. Some some things occurred in the offseason and all those type of things, but I'm always going to put this program first, put our players first, and uh, really sit back and evaluate things. Obviously, this is my first time doing both. Uh, you know, I I reached out to the guys, Venables being one before, you know, to really try to, you know, get some ideas from them and what they thought and all that type of stuff. But I I think you're always as a coach or a player within your scheme or your program, you're always evaluating how can we do it better. Uh and what's sustainable uh you know, and so I'm I'm not going to sit here and lie to you like, hey, has this been really easy as far as time management and all the things and what you want it to look like in all three phases and the ability when retention meetings are coming up, but you're still trying to game plan and all that. Absolutely. I mean, there's definitely a lot to it. So, uh, we'll definitely get together and Austin and I will sit down and what's this thing really look like, you know, need to look like moving forward and, uh, everything's definitely on the table. >> Okay, we'll wrap there. Thanks, guys. I appreciate it, fellas.
